# Research: action, pressure and impact for a narrative 2D companion game

Read-only pass. No files were edited. Code read in the worktree `.../scratchpad/wt-game/apps/game` (main.gd 1244 lines, m0_state.gd, m0_actor.gd, records_room.gd, containment_cage.gd, project.godot, assets/manifest.json, test function lists). Public rules read from `AGENT.md`. Private context read but only referred to abstractly below.

## 1. What the current build already gives us to build pressure on

| Hook | Where | Why it matters for action |

No shake exists yet. |
| Full-screen `IntroAlarm` and `IntroFade` ColorRects on the CanvasLayer | main.gd:18-19, 272-326 | Already used for a red alarm wash and fades in the opening; these are the "flash" layer for hits and hazards, free. |
| `RelaySpark` Line2D flashed by `_flash_relay_spark()` with a 0.48 s fade | main.gd:973-985 | The one existing "impact" effect. It is a tween on alpha only: no shake, no sound, no hit-stop. |

Any new hazard flags would need `SAVE_VERSION` 4 and `from_dict` validation. |
| Headless test harness: `_tap(action)`, `_walk_to(actor, x)`, `_wait_until(cond, frames)` | tests/m0_scene_test.gd:312-366, chapter_scene_test.gd:180-213 | A chase or hazard beat is headless-testable as "walk, wait N frames, assert state/position". |
| Settings glue already exposes volume sliders and remapping (`game_settings.gd`) | main.gd:406-475 | A "screen shake" / "reduced motion" toggle slots next to FPS/resolution. |

Gaps relevant to "boom": no audio pipeline at all (no AudioStreamPlayer nodes in main.gd), no particles, no camera shake, no time-scale manipulation, no hazard or fail state, no hit-stop. Everything today is a tween on a sprite or a ColorRect.

## 2. What the referenced games actually do (cited)

### Inside / Limbo (Playdead): trial and death, teach safe then kill
- Limbo's team called its loop "trial and death": puzzles assume the player will die first, and the gruesome death animations exist to steer players away from unworkable solutions. Lead designer Jeppe Carlsen's GDC Europe 2010 example puzzle has only three elements (switch panel, electrified floor, chain); the goal is immediately obvious and the challenge is timing and ordering. Their process: "first assume the player is their own worst enemy," then scale back as if designing for a friend. Checkpoints are frequent so deaths are learning moments, not penalties. (Wikipedia, Limbo development section; the GameSpot GDC write-up and a Playdead ex-staff interview were in search results but returned 403 to fetch.)
- Inside's first eight minutes teach every core verb with no text: the hazard appears in a safe form first (a wall you drag a box to climb) and only later under pressure (the dog chase, where "you have to move, and now!"). Cues are environmental (a fridge that "stands out via its placement and contrasting color"; a cough sound for oxygen). The write-up's pacing rule: "If you pressure them too often you risk losing them, and same if you have too many slow areas." (Game Developer, "Inside - Teaching through Level Design".)

### Little Nightmares (Tarsier): hide, wait, timing, known threat
- The fear lives in "the moment right before being caught, when the tension is still building"; "the whereabouts of the monsters are almost always known", so dread comes from waiting inches from a visible threat, not from surprise. Scale (levers too high, drawers as stairs) sells vulnerability. Sound "magnifies the atmosphere". (Hypercritic review.)
- Tarsier on companions for solo play: the AI companion must neither make players feel "led through the game like a rollercoaster" nor become "an irritating deadweight". Monster ideas are "connected by the loosest of threads" so they stay suggestive. Difficulty target: "challenge but not to the point of frustration". (Cubed3 Tarsier interview. The Unreal Engine LN2 interview was in search results but 403 on fetch.)

### Oddworld: New 'n' Tasty: stealth, possession, bounded retry
- Abe cannot attack; progress is wit (switches), stealth (shadows) and confrontation by possessing a Slig after a ~5 s chant. Possessed enemies can shoot and use switches but cannot jump, so the borrowed body is a different verb set, not a power-up. Companions "will literally keep on running into hazards or enemies unless you specifically tell them to 'wait'". (Destructoid review.)
- The remake keeps QuikSave and adds denser checkpoints so "the most any player would have to redo is a maximum length of three screens"; difficulty modes change Abe's health and enemy reaction times. (Wikipedia, New 'n' Tasty.) That is the closest published number to "retry without losing more than the current beat".

### Trine (Frozenbyte): physics as a gate, not decoration
- "most puzzles and situations can be solved with any character, or any two characters"; physics objects are not eye candy because you cannot advance without them; the safety net is "a checkpoint system that resurrects all characters, respawn points when you die". Difficulty came from "playtesting the game a lot! It's a very iterative and uncontrolled process". (Game Developer interview.)

### The Last Guardian (Ueda): companion agency and protection beats
- Boy and Trico "can only communicate via gestures, motion, and reactions"; the opening is removing spears from Trico, bond first through a caring action, not exposition; "The boy doesn't possess combat skills, so you need to work together with Trico to overcome these threats." Combat is the proof of partnership, and the relationship has "dramatic peaks and troughs". (PlayStation Blog; already in AGENT.md references.)

### Brothers (Fares): the player's hands carry the relationship
- "The whole foundation of the idea is that you connect with your left hand to the bigger brother and right hand to the little brother." The two have different abilities; the ending's beat is mechanical (pressing the dead brother's button to find strength). Fares kept introducing new mechanics ("Why not?") so no interaction became routine; co-op would have broken the metaphor ("rather cut my hands"). (Game Informer Afterwords; Shacknews.)

### Dead Cells / Katana ZERO / Hollow Knight: how hits feel good
- Motion Twin: "it's mostly because of the satisfaction of the controls... we put a lot of effort into the feedback". The GDC 2019 talk "Dead Cells: What the F*n!?" is about controls, player feedback, particles and "making players' lives easier" while staying hard; the control tricks it covers are coyote time and input buffering. (Shacknews; GDC news; Class Central listing.)
- Katana ZERO (Justin Stander): "You have to make the engine flawless. No bugs"; controls must be "an extension of the player"; the goal is a game where "you always feel like it's your fault not the game's fault so you want to try one more time"; music slows with slow motion. Each slice is sound + brief screen flash + subtle shake, and the game exposes hit-pause percentage and shake intensity as settings. (GameRevolution interview; Wayline weapon-feel article; search snippet on settings.)
- Hollow Knight: no first-party Team Cherry quote on hit freeze was fetchable (the cohorted interview returned 403). What is documented: millisecond-level input registration, readable enemy silhouettes, the Soul risk/heal trade-off, and audio EQ that changes with surface/biome (InGameNews). Player thread: shake fires as "an indicator that something is happening (usually dangerous)", caused headaches for some, and had no toggle, which players resented. Treat that as the accessibility warning.

### Game feel numbers (Vlambeer, Sakurai, SF2, Godot recipe)
- Nuclear Throne pistol, per Jan Willem Nijman (30 fps, 320x240): sound on frame 0; camera kicks back 6 px from the aim point; +4 screenshake that "degenerates quickly"; weapon sprite kick 2 px then snaps back; first bullet frame is a circle (fake muzzle flash); on impact: hit sound + material sound + character sound, enemy pushed 3 px/frame, hit animation starts with a white frame then two "ouch" frames, and a 10-20 ms screen freeze. Framing: game feel is "the tactility of a feedback loop that just works", a craft, not magic. (Infovore, "Making Game Feel".)
- Sakurai on hitstop: duration scales with damage with a hard cap; some attacks get extra (Marth's tip); both attacker and victim vibrate, horizontally when grounded and vertically in the air; vibration starts large and decays; the attacker keeps moving imperceptibly during the freeze; vibration amplitude scales with camera distance. (Source Gaming translation of Famitsu column.) Street Fighter II froze both characters for about 10 frames on hit; without hitstop "it's harder to tell a hit occurred". (Critpoints.)
- "Juice it or lose it" defines juice as "maximum output for minimum input": tween, squash/stretch, shake, particles, sound layered on an unchanged simulation. (Game Developer video post.)
- Godot shake recipe: a `trauma` 0..1 that decays (`decay = 0.8`/s), `amount = pow(trauma, 2 or 3)`, `max_offset = Vector2(100, 75)`, `max_roll = 0.1` rad, sampled from noise rather than random, applied to `Camera2D.offset` and `rotation`. (KidsCanCode Godot 4 recipe.) Eiserloh's GDC 2016 camera talk: use both translational and rotational shake in 2D. Godot docs: `offset` is "useful for looking around or camera shake animations" and may exceed limits.
- Godot audio: `AudioStreamGenerator` + `push_frame()` works from GDScript but the docs warn it is "best used from C# or from a compiled language" and to drop mix_rate to 11025 or 22050 Hz in GDScript. Implication for this project: generate short PCM clips once at startup into `AudioStreamWAV` (code-only provenance, logged in the manifest) rather than streaming in `_process`.

### Horror pacing
- Silent Hill f (Al Yang, GDC): players who say they want to be scared "really mean is they want to feel tense"; tension is anticipation and build-up; jump scares numb; hiding concrete numbers matters because "a large part of the tension of horror games relies on giving the player incomplete information"; a deliberate "system breaker" release lets players shatter tension on their own terms so they are not exhausted. (GSMGO summary of the talk.)
- Frictional (Thomas Grip): ease players in from the familiar, slow build so a "single (or just few) peaks of terror" land; combat makes players "miss many of the subtle cues"; "players might be safe, they can never be sure"; horror gets personal when it is about its effect on other characters. (Shacknews; Game Developer IGF interview.)
- Left 4 Dead's Director: "things would slow down, things would get quiet, and then things would go batshit crazy"; "You can't appreciate the action unless you have some inaction." (Shacknews, Evolve/L4D.)

## 3. Distilled rules (14)

1. **Show the hazard safe before it is lethal.** Introduce the vent, shutter or pursuer once where it cannot hurt (Inside's box wall; Limbo's three-element puzzle where the goal is obvious and only timing is unknown). The player's first death should be on a thing they already recognised.
2. **A readable chase has one input, a visible threat and a visible goal.** Hold-right (or hold-left) is the whole verb; the pursuer or hazard front is always on screen or audible; the exit is marked by contrast (color/light/label, like Inside's fridge). Speed ratio creates the "move, now" without instructions. Never add a second simultaneous input on mobile.
3. **Death costs one beat, never more.** Oddworld's remake bound redo to about three screens; Limbo checkpoints before every puzzle. Here: fail resets to the last safe point or the start of the current beat with no save write and no story state loss.
4. **Make the death itself informative.** Limbo's gruesome deaths steer players from wrong answers. The fail animation should point at the cause (the vent that caught you, the shutter edge), then cut to retry within a second.
5. **Failure must read as the player's fault.** Katana ZERO: flawless engine, controls as extension; Dead Cells: coyote time and input buffering. For a game with no jump, the equivalent is a generous USE window, no input eaten by UI, and hazards whose collision matches their art.
6. **Alternate pressure and quiet.** Inside, L4D and Frictional all say the same thing: contrast is the pacing tool; aim for one real peak per room and a quiet beat with WOLF after it (AGENT.md already asks for this).
7. **Tension is anticipation plus incomplete information.** Known threat position (Little Nightmares), unknown timing; no visible counters for the dangerous thing (Silent Hill f). A countdown you can hear but not read beats a timer bar.
8. **Give the player a release valve they control.** Silent Hill f's "system breaker". In this game the valve can be the engineer's own act (slamming a breaker, sealing a door) so the "boom" is caused, not watched.
9. **A companion's intervention is earned by a prior caring or shared action, and shown in motion.** Last Guardian: bond first, gestures not words, cooperation proven in danger. The existing `_react_as_wolf` lean (main.gd:958-970) is the right instinct; the intervention beat needs WOLF to physically do something that changes state (block, pull, hold) rather than a line.
10. **The companion must neither lead nor be deadweight, and must stay optional.** Tarsier's rollercoaster/deadweight warning plus Trine's "any character can solve it": every protection beat needs the engineer-only route (a slower, scarier manual path), and WOLF's help is a choice he makes, not a prompt the player presses.
11. **Impact is a fixed stack fired by one state change, in this order:** sound (frame 0) → white/flash frame on the thing hit → hit-stop 10-20 ms (2-10 frames; scale with severity, cap it) → camera kick toward/away plus shake that decays fast → knockback/displacement → particles/debris → secondary material/character sounds. All of it reads from the real state flag so there is never fake feedback.
12. **Shake is trauma-driven, noise-sampled, applied to `Camera2D.offset`, and capped.** `shake = trauma^2`, decay ~0.8/s, small amplitudes at 960x540 (think 4-8 px, not 100), translational plus a little roll, scaled by zoom; expose a reduce/disable toggle (Katana ZERO does; Hollow Knight's lack of one drew complaints).
13. **Hit-stop vibrates both parties, decays, and keeps a sliver of motion.** Sakurai: horizontal vibration on ground, vertical in air, large-to-small, attacker never fully frozen. In Godot: freeze via `Engine.time_scale` or per-node `process_mode` for a few frames while a tiny sprite jitter continues.
14. **Sound carries the feel; layer three sounds per hit and let music react.** Vlambeer's action + material + character layering; Katana ZERO slows the music in slow-mo; Hollow Knight EQs by surface. With no audio yet, procedurally generated clips (noise bursts, sine thumps, filtered clicks) baked once into `AudioStreamWAV` are enough to prove the stack and carry clean provenance.

## 4. How this maps to the constraints (research notes, not a decision)

- **Bounded slice shape that fits the rules and the two rooms:** a pressure beat in the corridor between the relay and the safe point, using existing verbs. Example shape consistent with the rules: the seal opening triggers a coolant vent cycle (hazard shown first as a harmless hiss/steam puff from the same `RelaySpark`/ColorRect layer, then lethal on a visible rhythm); the engineer must hold-right through it between pulses; WOLF, if the relay memory is cooperative, can choose to stand in the vent's path (authored protection shown as motion, state flag `vent_blocked_by_wolf`), while the engineer-only route is timing the pulses; a miss triggers the impact stack (flash, hit-stop, shake, thump), a short fall animation, and a retry from the vent entrance with no save written. The user's "boom" is the vent burst and the shutter slam, both caused by player-visible state.
- **Godot nodes only:** Camera2D.offset shake, Tween, ColorRect flash, GPUParticles2D/CPUParticles2D (CPU variant is safer under GL Compatibility on mobile), Area2D for hazard volumes, StaticBody2D for shutters, AudioStreamPlayer with AudioStreamWAV built in code, `Engine.time_scale` for hit-stop.
- **Saves:** a fail/retry loop that resets to the existing checkpoint needs no save change; adding new persisted flags means bumping `SAVE_VERSION` to 4 and extending `from_dict` validation (m0_state.gd:147-237).
- **Headless proof:** extend `m0_scene_test.gd` with "walk into hazard during active pulse -> position reset, state unchanged, no file write" and "WOLF blocks when memory is DISCLOSE; engineer passes on timing when PRESS". Feel claims (shake amplitude, hit-stop length) still require hands-on play per AGENT.md.
- **Mobile:** hold-to-move plus USE covers rules 2 and 8; no third input needed.

## 5. Source quality notes

Fetched directly and used: Wikipedia (Limbo development; New 'n' Tasty), Game Developer (Inside teaching; Trine interview; Amnesia IGF interview; Juice it or lose it video post), Hypercritic and Cubed3 (Little Nightmares/Tarsier), Destructoid (NnT), PlayStation Blog (Last Guardian), Game Informer and Shacknews (Brothers), Shacknews (Dead Cells; L4D/Evolve; Frictional), GDC news (Dead Cells talk), GameRevolution and Wayline (Katana ZERO), Infovore (Nuclear Throne numbers), Source Gaming and Critpoints (hitstop), KidsCanCode (Godot shake), Godot 4.7 docs (Camera2D, AudioStreamGenerator), GSMGO (Silent Hill f talk), Steam thread (Hollow Knight shake), InGameNews (Hollow Knight). 
Blocked (403/503) and therefore only known through search snippets: GameSpot's Carlsen GDC Europe piece, the Unreal Engine Little Nightmares II interview, the cohorted Team Cherry interview, GiantBomb "A Tale of One Game". The Hollow Knight developer-voice gap is the weakest point in this set.

## 3. The authored-event pattern new beats should follow (m0_state.gd)

- Memory record: `record_choice()` (40-51) writes `{event_id, choice_id, selected_text, context, sequence, observed_by}`; `CHOICE_TEXT` is the only accepted text; duplicates rejected.
- Transitions are guard methods that return `bool` or a short result code string and are idempotent: `arm_breaker()` (54-58), `activate_power(actor) -> "not_ready"|"already_open"|"refused"|"cooperate"|"fallback"|"invalid_actor"` (61-75), `reach_checkpoint()`, `enter_records()`, `preserve_*()`, `complete_chapter()`. The scene (`main.gd`) only reads the code and plays feedback; it never mutates state fields directly.
- `to_dict()`/`from_dict()` validate every cross-field invariant (`door_open == (route != "")`, `cooperate ⇒ DISCLOSE`, records ⇒ checkpoint, mirror ⇒ purge). New fields: bump `SAVE_VERSION` to 4, default them for v≤3, validate under `if data["version"] >= 4`.
- Transient UI flags (`relay_refused`, `wolf_heading_to_relay`, `waiting_for_choice`) live in `main.gd` and are reset by `_new_game`/`_load_game`; they are not saved. Hazard phase, drone position, countdown remaining and "hidden" belong in this transient tier, not the save.
- WOLF's choices are deterministic rules on state (e.g. `memory.choice_id == DISCLOSE` gates cooperation) with an authored visible action (`_react_as_wolf`, `autonomous_target_x`) and a guaranteed engineer fallback (second USE = bypass, 785-822).

2. **`SfxBank` procedural audio** on the `Effects` bus, three or four generated clips, one manifest entry, drop the "no audio tracks yet" note. Hook breaker arm, relay contact, choice confirm. Test: clip bytes deterministic, bus name, plays.

- Debris (booms): amount 12, lifetime 0.9, velocity 150-260, spread 60, gravity (0,900), angular_velocity 200-500, scale 3-5, color `#2b3238`.
- Steam/coolant vent (continuous, `one_shot = false`): amount 40, lifetime 1.2, direction (0,-1), spread 12, velocity 120-180, gravity (0,-60), scale 6→18 via `scale_amount_curve`, color `#bfe8ff` alpha 0.35→0; toggle `emitting` with the vent state so the visual is the state.

**Squash and stretch.** Tween `body_sprite.scale` (Sprite2D scales around its own position, so set `body_sprite.offset` so the feet are the pivot, or accept the 5-15 px sprite offset already used): impact (1.12, 0.88) in 0.06 s then back to (1,1) in 0.12 s `TRANS_CUBIC/EASE_OUT`; start-moving stretch (0.94, 1.06) 0.05 s; landing after knockback (1.15, 0.85). Run it `parallel()` to the existing lean tween, which animates `position`/`rotation_degrees`, so they do not fight; kill and reset in `_sync_scene()` like the lean tween.

**Controller rumble.** `Input.start_joy_vibration(device, weak_magnitude, strong_magnitude, duration = 0)`; `stop_joy_vibration(device)`. macOS 11+ only, and over USB only major-brand pads except Xbox One/Series (macOS limitation), so never rely on it. Use device 0 when `controller_active`. Starting values: click/beep weak 0.15 / strong 0 / 0.06 s; spark 0.3 / 0.5 / 0.15 s; scald 0.4 / 0.6 / 0.15 s; boom 0.5 / 0.9 / 0.25 s.

**Mobile haptics.** `Input.vibrate_handheld(duration_ms = 500, amplitude = -1.0)`; Android needs the `VIBRATE` permission in the export preset; amplitude needs iOS 13+; web ignores amplitude and Safari/Firefox-Android do not support it; device "do not disturb"/settings can suppress it. Starting values: click 25 ms / 0.3; spark 60 / 0.5; scald 90 / 0.8; boom 160 / 1.0. Gate on `touch_enabled`.

Add one "Vibration" toggle to Settings later (both rumble and haptics) and keep every effect readable with it off; the game's "basic controls always reliable" rule applies to feedback too.

## 4. Sound

**Players and buses.** `AudioStreamPlayer` is non-positional (UI, beeps, booms, music); `AudioStreamPlayer2D` attenuates and pans by screen position relative to the listener (default: screen centre), with `max_distance` (2000 default), `attenuation`, `panning_strength` (project base × 1.0), `max_polyphony`. For this game: booms, beeps, clicks and the scald on a pool of 3-4 `AudioStreamPlayer`s (`max_polyphony` up to 4 if one node) on bus `Effects`; vent hiss and relay spark on `AudioStreamPlayer2D` (max_distance ≈ 900, attenuation 1.5) so they sit left/right as the camera pans; music later on `Music`; any future WOLF TTS on `Voice`. The runtime buses already exist with sliders. Add a hard limiter to Master via `AudioServer.add_bus_effect(0, AudioEffectLimiter.new())` (docs recommend a limiter last on Master to prevent clipping; stacked booms will clip without it). A muffled "stunned" moment after a scald = `AudioEffectLowPassFilter` on `Effects` (`cutoff_hz` default 2000, range 1-20500; use ~600 for 0.4 s) toggled with `set_bus_effect_enabled`. Headless CI uses the dummy audio driver; `play()` is safe to call.

**Procedural SFX, recommended approach: bake, don't stream.** `AudioStreamGenerator` is a real-time stream with `buffer_length` 0.5 s default (latency) and the docs warn it is CPU-heavy from GDScript (suggest 11025-22050 Hz). For one-shot SFX it is better to synthesise once at `_ready` into an `AudioStreamWAV` (`format = FORMAT_16_BITS`, `mix_rate` 22050 or 44100, `stereo = false`, `data` = little-endian signed 16-bit PCM) with a seeded `RandomNumberGenerator`, then play it normally: zero trigger latency, deterministic, no third-party asset, and the buffer is unit-testable. Keep the generator pattern (`get_stream_playback()`, `get_frames_available()`, `push_frame(Vector2)`, 22050 Hz in the official demo) only for a continuous hiss if you want it live; a 1 s looped baked clip (`loop_mode = LOOP_FORWARD`) is simpler. Use `AudioStreamRandomizer` (`random_pitch` 1.08, `random_volume_offset_db` 2) around footsteps/clicks so repeats do not sound mechanical. `save_to_wav("user://...")` lets you audition and archive clips for the register.

Packing and filters (load-bearing formulas):
```gdscript
# 16-bit mono packing
var bytes := PackedByteArray(); bytes.resize(frames * 2)
bytes.encode_s16(i * 2, int(clampf(sample, -1.0, 1.0) * 32767.0))
# one-pole low-pass per sample (dt = 1.0 / mix_rate); high-pass = x - low
var alpha := dt / (1.0 / (TAU * cutoff_hz) + dt); low += alpha * (x - low)
```
Recipes (amplitudes before the Master limiter; all with a 3-8 ms linear attack to avoid clicks):
- **Beep / terminal confirm** (breaker arm, trace copied, valve click): sine 880 Hz, or a two-step 660→880 Hz, 90-120 ms, exponential decay tau 40 ms, amplitude 0.35. Square-ish variant (`sign(sin)` mixed 30 %) reads as "terminal".
- **Spark crackle** (relay, conduit): 250-350 ms of white noise multiplied by 4-7 random gate windows of 6-18 ms, high-passed (x minus a 1.2 kHz low-pass), plus a 60 ms sine "zap" sweeping 2400→500 Hz; amplitude 0.5, decay tau 120 ms.
- **Boom** (pipe rupture, hatch slam): white noise through a low-pass whose cutoff sweeps 500→70 Hz over 600 ms, summed with a sine sub sweeping 75→35 Hz over 250 ms, overall exponential decay tau 0.35 s, 1.0-1.2 s long, soft-clip with `tanh(1.8 * s)` for weight, peak 0.9. Boom 2 = same with tau 0.5 s and a second noise layer 80 ms later.
- **Scald / vent hit**: boom-lite (tau 0.15, 0.4 s) plus a crackle layer; amplitude 0.7.
- **Hiss loop**: 1 s of noise low-passed at 3 kHz with slow 2 Hz amplitude wobble, loop, amplitude 0.25; `pitch_scale` 1.15 in beat 3.
- **Footsteps**: 50-70 ms noise burst low-passed at 600 Hz (concrete) with tau 20 ms, amplitude 0.3; trigger every 46-50 px of travel while `is_on_floor()` and `absf(velocity.x) > 1` (≈4 steps/s at 190 px/s), through a randomizer. Give WOLF a lower, two-tap variant (paws).

**CC0 fallback sources** (only if the procedural set sounds thin; nothing paid or unlicensed):
- **Kenney**: "Impact Sounds" (130 files, Creative Commons CC0), "Sci-Fi Sounds" (70, CC0), "Interface Sounds" (100, CC0); each pack page states CC0 and ships a `License.txt` in the zip (the site-root license URL now 404s, so cite the per-pack page and bundled file). Credit is appreciated, not required.
- **OpenGameArt.org**: filter search by licence and use only CC0 entries; their suggested credit format is "[asset] by [author] licensed [license]: [url]" (not required for CC0, but it is exactly what the register wants).
- **Freesound.org**: advanced search → licence filter → CC0 only; the FAQ confirms CC0 sounds may be used commercially without credit and the site keeps a per-account attribution list; CC-BY-NC entries are off limits for a $4.99 release.
- CC0 1.0 itself: all copyright and related rights waived worldwide, commercial use and modification allowed, no attribution required; it does not waive trademark/patent/publicity rights and the deed is not the legal code.

**What `apps/game/assets/manifest.json` must record** (its `future_entry_fields`): `asset_id`, `path`, `source_or_tool`, `terms_reference`, `rights_review_status`, `modifications`, `implementation_status`, plus the `source_reference` the existing entries carry. For a Kenney/OGA/Freesound clip: pack or sound name, author, exact URL and sound ID, download date, "CC0 1.0 Universal" with the deed link, and any trimming/pitching done. For procedural clips: one entry per module (e.g. `procedural-sfx-v1`) naming the script, the seed, the generation parameters, "generated by project code, no third-party source", and noting whether the clips are covered by the code licence (the register currently says art is not covered by the GPL; decide the same question for code-generated audio explicitly). Also update the register `status` line ("no audio acquired"), the Settings note, the in-game credits, the public credits/asset-rights pages and the changelog in the same PR (AGENT.md).

## 5. Priority order for the first "impact" pass (before the new room)

1. **Audio foundation** (half a day): `ProceduralSfx` module that bakes the beep, click, spark, boom, scald, hiss and footstep clips into `AudioStreamWAV`s; a 4-voice `AudioStreamPlayer` pool on `Effects`; Master limiter; headless test on buffer length/peak; Settings note and register updated.
2. **Hook existing moments** (one day): beep on breaker arm and both Records copies; spark crackle + 0.35 trauma + spark `CPUParticles2D` at the relay (blue for WOLF, orange for the bypass); seal-rise boom-lite + dust + 0.5 trauma + rumble/haptic when the door opens; soft thud + 0.25 trauma at the opening seal breaking; footsteps for both actors. This alone turns "walk, interact, choose" into something that answers back.
3. **Camera shake + hit-stop utilities** with reset in every scene-sync path and a test for `time_scale`/`offset` restoration.
4. **Rumble and haptics** gated on `controller_active` / `touch_enabled`, with a Settings toggle.
5. **Squash/stretch** on the engineer's start/stop and WOLF's accept/refuse lean.
6. **PRESSURE LINE room** (§2) with save v4, the only fail state, both WOLF outcomes, and the two booms.
7. Only then: chromatic pulse shader, music bus content, reduced-motion setting.

Caveats: nothing above is validated by play; every feel claim needs the route played in one window with a separate test save, and exports/devices (especially haptics permissions and macOS rumble limits) need their own checks.

beats.goal: Survive the rupture and understand the new hazard (the boom).
beats.action: Walk right across the trigger line at x 420 (not a button, just movement).
beats.response: Hit-stop: Engine.time_scale 0.05 for 70 ms (restored by a one-shot SceneTreeTimer that ignores time scale). White-blue flash on IntroAlarm 90 ms then red wash 0.13 alpha for 2 s. Camera trauma 0.9 (~8 px shake decaying over 0.7 s). Boom SFX (sub sine 55 to 30 Hz 0.5 s plus lowpass noise burst), rumble strong 0.9 for 0.3 s, Input.vibrate_handheld(180). Vents A and B start cycling: warn 0.6 s (strip blinks amber, particles ramp, rising hiss), burst 1.1 s (strip red, 110-px steam column, loud hiss, 56x110 hurtbox enabled), idle 1.8 s (strip dim blue, hurtbox disabled). Phase offset B = 1.75 s so they are never both idle for long. WOLF barks once and backs away from vent A on his own (authored target 470).
beats.result: gallery_stage = 2, block_spawned = true, vent_clock = 0 and running. Beat anchor B recorded after the block settles (block at 520, engineer at trigger, vents at clock 0). Fails from here return to anchor B.

beats.goal: Get the block under the far ledge: push it across live vent A and vent B without being in a burst.
beats.action: Hold right into the block. The engineer pushes it at 90 px/s (block is a CharacterBody2D on layer 4; human mask 2|4 and, on a slide collision with the block, sets block.push_velocity; WOLF mask 2 so he walks behind it). Releasing the stick stops the push instantly. Jumping over a grate alone in its idle window is also possible (177 px airtime arc clears 56 px) but the block cannot jump, so the push must be timed.
beats.response: Pushing: looping brown-noise scrape while block.velocity.x != 0, 1 px shake while pushing, sparks under the block every 20 px of travel. When the block AABB fully covers a grate, that vent is capped: hurtbox disabled, steam particles stop, hiss muffles to a rattle, strip goes amber. Pushing on uncaps it (state resumes from the live clock, no cheat). The engineer's 28-px body is exposed for about 0.93 s crossing a grate at push speed, inside a 1.8 s idle window, so the player has to start the push on the warn-to-idle edge. WOLF, up on the far ledge already (he jumped it on his own; he can clear 120 px, the engineer cannot), paces and barks on each vent's warn phase after the first fail, a readable audio cue.
beats.result: block.position.x within 12 px of 790 (parked against the ledge face) sets gallery_stage = 3 and records beat anchor C. Any burst contact triggers the fail beat (see fail_and_retry).

beats.goal: Climb the block and the ledge, then kill the line: WOLF's choice happens here.
beats.action: When the engineer first reaches x 700 or the block reaches 790 (whichever first), the choice prompt appears once: 1 "Pull the shutoff if it's safe for you" / 2 "Leave it, I'll crank it myself". If the breaker-memory choice was the disclosure line and the player picks 1, WOLF pulls it: the wheel turns on its own, both vents die, the pressure drops out of the room. If the memory choice was the press-without-warning line, WOLF refuses the live valve (he already told them once) and instead crouches at the ledge edge as a visible marker of the safe landing spot. Engineer path regardless: JUMP onto the block (64 px, within the 98 px apex), JUMP to the ledge (56 px more), walk to the wheel, hold USE.
beats.response: Each 0.35 s of held USE is one crank: wheel sprite rotates 90 degrees, a metallic click, rumble weak 0.25 for 0.08 s, 2 px shake. Crank 1 kills vent B (steam dies, strip green, hiss stops). Crank 2 kills vent A. Crank 3 unlocks the exit hatch with a heavy clunk. Releasing USE keeps cranks already made. If WOLF pulled it, the engineer arriving sees the wheel already green and the hatch already open, and the climb is a quiet victory lap.
beats.result: gallery_shutoff_by = "wolf" or "human", shutoff_cranks 0..3, vents off; gallery_stage = 4; autosave written. The choice is recorded in the authored memory style as a second remembered event (who asked what, what WOLF chose, observed_by both).

beats.goal: Leave together; short aftermath.
beats.action: USE at the exit hatch on the ledge (x 910).
beats.response: Hatch slides with a hydraulic hiss and a soft thud, camera settles, red wash fades. One quiet exchange: WOLF's line depends on who pulled the shutoff and how many times the engineer got hit (zero hits, one, or more; no penalty, just a different sentence). Top card ARCHIVE TRAIL AHEAD.

options.wolf_role: WOLF traverses what the engineer cannot: he bounds the 72-px step on entry (teaching the jump by example) and later clears the 120-px ledge on his own authored path, so the engineer sees where the room wants them to end up. He does not push (the block only responds to the engineer's slide collision). At the shutoff he chooses: with the disclosure memory from the breaker he will pull the valve when asked, which turns the timed push into a calm one (a relief reward for earlier honesty, not a progress gate). With the press-without-warning memory he refuses the live valve again and instead marks the safe landing spot and barks the vent rhythm after the first fail. Refusal costs nothing: the engineer-only path is always jump the step, time the push, climb the block, crank the wheel. Every WOLF action is a deterministic rule on existing state plus an authored visible motion, exactly like the relay and mirror beats.
options.engineer_fallback: The full route needs no WOLF action: jump the step (72 px under the 98 px apex), push the block across both vents by timing the 1.8 s idle windows, jump block then ledge (64 px then 56 px), hold USE for three cranks, USE the hatch. If WOLF refuses or is ignored the only difference is the vents stay live during the push. Basic move, jump and USE never get removed by fear, refusal or the choice prompt (the prompt only swaps touch buttons, as today).
options.fail_and_retry: Contact with an enabled burst hurtbox calls _fail_beat(): time_scale 0.05 for 70 ms, white-blue flash, trauma 0.8, a procedural steam-slam sound, rumble strong 0.8 for 0.3 s, controls off, the engineer tweened 40 px away from the vent with a stagger squash, 0.7 s hold, then restore the most recent transient beat anchor (A: room entry, B: post-boom with block at 520 and vent clock 0, C: block parked at 790). Anchors live in main.gd transient state, never in the save, so a fail never rewrites or corrupts progress; Continue still loads the last autosave (gallery entry or shutoff done). Nothing beyond the current beat is lost: a fail during the push restores the block to where that beat started, not to the entry hatch. gallery_fails counts up only for WOLF's optional rhythm barks and the aftermath line; there is no lives counter, no timer penalty, no locked door.

options.name: BLOWBACK: Service Junction (tools and sabotage slice)
options.pitch: A third 960-px room right after the Records exit where the Director's lockdown has sealed the service line to Archive. The engineer has no weapon, only the building's own plumbing and power: overpressure the coolant line and crank a valve to blow a sealed door, drop a suspended coolant tank from a maintenance arm onto the purge sentry that the first boom woke up, then dump the overload into the junction box to pop the exit bolt and kill the lights. Three real, loud, state-changing booms in about three minutes, each one with a timing window and a blast zone the player has to respect. WOLF scouts ahead, reads the pressure, and, if he trusts the engineer, baits the sentry under the arm; every tool is engineer-operated and every boom has an engineer-only timing path. Fail is a knockdown and a reload of the beat's own autosave, never more than ~20 s lost.
options.where: New chapter_id "junction" (SAVE_VERSION 4) entered from the Records exit at x 830 after complete_chapter() (replaces today's 'The Archive trail is next' card with a real transition, same pattern as enter_records()). Same 960x540 canvas, same floor at y 440, same camera clamp, same corridor-style station layout. Left to right: entry hatch x 80; OVERLOAD BREAKER x 200; relief vent (floor grate) x 300; VALVE WHEEL x 420; SEALED PRESSURE DOOR x 480 (StaticBody2D 56x132 on layer 2, same as the corridor door); rubble line x 540 after the blow; ARM PANEL x 570; sentry lane x 600..840; suspended coolant tank on a maintenance arm at x 700 (tank rest y 250, lands at y 410); JUNCTION BOX / sentry dock x 800; EXIT BOLT PANEL x 850; exit hatch x 880. All within the existing 40..920 actor clamp and the 406.8..553.2 camera clamp.

beats.goal: Beat 0 - Entry. Understand the room: the line to Archive is sealed and something is humming behind the door.
beats.action: Walk in from the left (hold-to-move). No button needed.
beats.response: Top card 'SERVICE JUNCTION / CLEAR THE LINE'. WOLF runs ahead on an authored autonomous_target_x to the sealed door (x 440), sniffs the seam, backs off two steps with the existing lean tween (accepting=false) and a short procedural growl. The door's seam glows amber and a low pump hum sits under the room. Status line: WOLF reads pressure behind the door and says the breaker on the left feeds it.
beats.result: state.chapter_id = "junction", all four junction flags false, positions captured, autosave A written via _save_progress(). WOLF returns to follow_target. Human controlled.

beats.goal: Beat 1 - Build pressure and crank the valve before the relief vent lets go, then get clear of the door.
beats.action: USE at the OVERLOAD BREAKER (x 200) arms the line. Walk right past the relief vent (x 300) to the VALVE WHEEL (x 420) and HOLD USE: every 0.4 s held is one real turn (3 turns needed). Then walk LEFT out of the blast zone (x < 360) before the 1.0 s fuse ends.
beats.response: On arm: breaker clunk, the pump hum rises in pitch and volume with the gauge (PressureLine.gauge 0..1 over 6 s), a drawn gauge needle beside the valve sweeps green to amber to red, and the relief vent at x 300 puffs steam harder as the gauge climbs (CPUParticles2D amount tied to gauge). Each crank turn: wheel sprite rotates 90 degrees, metallic click, weak rumble (0.2 for 0.08 s), one of three valve lights goes green. Turn 3: klaxon chirp x3, door seam strobes white, status 'SEAL CHARGED - CLEAR THE DOOR', fuse 1.0 s. If the gauge reaches 1.0 before turn 3: the relief vent BLOWS (small boom, trauma 0.5): the breaker trips (lights off, needs re-arm, gauge resets to 0); if the engineer is standing on the vent (x 250..350) they are knocked down (fail, see fail_and_retry), otherwise it is just a loud warning and a reset.
beats.result: Transient PressureLine state: idle -> building -> charged(3 turns) -> fuse -> blown. Releasing USE keeps turns already made. On fuse end, Beat 2 fires. Nothing is saved until the door is actually blown, so a trip or knockdown costs only this beat.

beats.goal: Beat 2 - BOOM 1: the door blows, and the noise wakes what was behind it.
beats.action: None: the fuse ends. The player's only job was to be outside x 360..540. If they are inside it when it goes, they are knocked down (fail).
beats.response: Hit-stop 70 ms (Engine.time_scale 0.05 via a PROCESS_MODE_ALWAYS timer), white flash 90 ms on IntroFade over a 300 ms red wash on IntroAlarm, camera trauma 1.0 (offset shake, ~10 px, 0.6 s decay), door_visual scale:y collapses as in _sync_door and a rubble Sprite/draw appears at x 540, two CPUParticles2D bursts (sparks and dust), strong rumble 0.8 for 0.25 s / vibrate_handheld(180), procedural boom (noise burst + 55->30 Hz sub). Half a second later: a servo whine and two red eye lights come up at x 820: the sentry wakes and starts to patrol. WOLF's ears go back, he holds at the rubble line and will not cross, growl loop low.
beats.result: state.door_blown = true, door collision shape disabled, autosave B written. Sentry brain enters 'patrol' (600..840 at 140 px/s). Status line names the new problem: a purge sentry is on the lane and the maintenance arm above it is holding a coolant tank.

beats.goal: Beat 3 - Cross the rubble and get to the ARM PANEL without the sentry tagging you; decide how the tank gets dropped.
beats.action: Step onto the rubble line (x 540): the choice prompt appears (player-paced; the sentry brain does not tick while waiting_for_choice). 1 'Draw it under the arm if you can stay clear' / 2 'Stay back. I'll time the drop.' Then walk into the lane to the ARM PANEL (x 570) while the sentry is at the far end, and watch its patrol.
beats.response: Choice 1 with memory.choice_id == DISCLOSE: WOLF accepts (lean tween, bark), lopes to x 740 and holds there; the sentry fixates on him and parks at x ~700 lunging (state 'fixated'). Choice 1 with PRESS memory: WOLF refuses on screen (lean back, growl, 'Not blind. Not again.') and stays at the rubble: the engineer gets the timing path. Choice 2: WOLF stays and watches. In the lane: the sentry's eye strip is amber while patrolling, snaps red with a rising servo whine when it detects the engineer (engineer in lane x > 545, within 180 px in its facing direction, and not standing in the panel alcove 556..584 which counts as cover), and chases at 230 px/s. Being touched = knockdown (fail). It loses the engineer 2.5 s after they leave the lane over the rubble and returns to patrol; it cannot cross x 540.
beats.result: Transient: wolf_baiting (bool), sentry brain state in {patrol, chase, fixated, down}. No save change. Engineer-only path is always available: time the drop on the patrol alone.

beats.goal: Beat 4 - BOOM 2: drop the tank on the sentry.
beats.action: At the ARM PANEL, tap USE when the sentry is under the tank (x within 44 px of 700). With WOLF baiting it is parked there; without him, the player reads the patrol (the tank's shadow on the floor is drawn as the target mark) and taps on the pass.
beats.response: USE: clamp release clack, the tank falls on a 0.45 s tween (gravity ease), cable goes slack. HIT: hit-stop 90 ms, white flash, trauma 1.0, cyan-white coolant burst particles, sentry sparks, keels over on a rotation tween, eye lights die, servo whine pitches down to silence; strong rumble; boom with a glassy top. MISS: dull clang, the tank dents and vents a coolant cloud at x 700 for 3 s (hazard Area2D, touching it = knockdown), the sentry snaps to red and chases the panel; the engineer must retreat left over the rubble (570 -> 540 is 30 px, it is fair but tight); the arm visibly rewinds the cable for 6 s with a winch sound and re-hangs the tank, so the player can try again without a reload. If WOLF was baiting and the drop missed, he breaks off and will not bait again this attempt (his choice; status says so), so the retry is the timing path.
beats.result: On hit: state.sentry_down = true, sentry becomes a static prop, autosave C. On miss: transient only (arm state 'rewinding' 6 s, sentry 'chase' then 'patrol'). A knockdown reloads autosave B with the tank re-hung and the sentry reset to the far end.

beats.goal: Beat 5 - BOOM 3 and aftermath: dump the overload into the junction box to pop the exit bolt, then leave in the dark.
beats.action: Walk to the EXIT BOLT PANEL (x 850), past the dead sentry and its dock. USE once: the panel routes the still-armed overload down the line into the junction box (x 800). Then USE at the exit hatch (x 880).
beats.response: Overload: 0.6 s rising electrical whine, then an arc flash (white flash 120 ms, trauma 0.8, spark particles out of the box), every room light and station light goes out (CanvasModulate tween to a dark blue over 0.4 s), the red IntroAlarm wash fades in at 0.1 and holds, the bolt drops with a heavy clank and the hatch slides open on a scale tween. Quiet aftermath, no hum anymore: WOLF's eye lights are the brightest thing in the room; he walks to the engineer, puts himself between them and the dark lane (authored autonomous_target_x = human.x + 48) and gives one short line about the sentry being the Director's answer, not a glitch. USE at the hatch: top card 'SERVICE LINE CLEARED' and the chapter-close camera move already used by Records.
beats.result: state.junction_dark = true then state.junction_cleared = true, autosave D. Human stays controlled throughout the aftermath (controls are never removed). Chapter close uses the existing chapter_close_active flow.

options.wolf_role: WOLF scouts, reads and holds; he never operates a tool. Beat 0: runs ahead and reads the pressure behind the door (authored autonomous_target_x, lean tween, growl). Beat 2: refuses to cross the rubble while the sentry is live, which marks the lane as dangerous without text. Beat 3/4: if the engineer disclosed the relay risk earlier (memory.choice_id == DISCLOSE, the same deterministic rule activate_power uses) and the player asks, WOLF chooses to bait the sentry under the arm and holds it there (sentry state 'fixated'); with PRESS memory he visibly refuses and stays back; if a drop misses while he is baiting he breaks off and will not bait again on that attempt. Beat 5: he positions himself between the engineer and the dark lane. Engineer-only fallback for every objective: the breaker, valve, arm panel and exit panel are all engineer stations; without WOLF the tank drop is a patrol-timing read on a drawn floor mark (sentry at 140 px/s, 88 px hit window = ~0.6 s of valid tap time per pass, with the arm rewinding for a retry on a miss). Nothing requires WOLF, and asking him costs nothing when he refuses.
options.engineer_fallback: Every tool is engineer-operated and no boom depends on WOLF: (1) overload breaker + valve crank + run-clear is pure engineer timing; (2) the tank drop can be timed on the sentry's patrol pass alone (floor shadow mark shows the landing x; a miss rewinds the arm in 6 s so the beat retries in place without a reload); (3) the exit overload is a single USE. If WOLF refuses or breaks off, the status line says so and points at the mark, exactly as the relay bypass does today.
options.fail_and_retry: One fail path, _fail_beat(reason): knockdown sources are the relief vent blowing with the engineer on it, standing in the door blast zone at fuse end, sentry contact, or the coolant cloud after a miss. Sequence: hit-stop 60 ms, red flash, human sprite rotates ~70 degrees and slides 30 px with a thud and strong rumble, controls off for 1.1 s, IntroFade to black 0.4 s, then _load_game() from the single save slot (which is the autosave at the start of the current beat: A at entry, B after the door blows, C after the sentry is down) and a status line that names what happened and what to change ('The relief vent caught you. Crank before the gauge goes red, then clear the door.'). Transient state resets on load: PressureLine idle, breaker un-armed, tank re-hung, sentry at the far end in patrol, wolf_baiting false, Engine.time_scale 1.0, camera offset zero. Loss is bounded to the current beat (~10-20 s). No fail counter is saved and WOLF's memory and the Records flags are untouched; a knockdown is treated as 'you were there, it hurt', never as a moral or story penalty.

final_options.pitch: A third 960-px room right after the Records exit. The service line to the Archive is sealed and something hums behind the door. The engineer has no weapon, only the building: overload the coolant line and crank a valve to blow the sealed door, drop a hanging coolant tank on the purge sentry the blast woke up, then dump the overload into the exit bolt. beats.goal: Reach the ARM PANEL without being tagged and decide how the tank gets dropped.
beats.action: Step on the rubble line (x 540): the choice prompt appears (the sentry brain does not tick during waiting_for_choice). 1 'Draw it under the arm if you can stay clear' / 2 'Stay back, I'll time it.' Then walk to x 570 while the sentry is at the far end.
beats.response: Choice 1 with DISCLOSE memory: WOLF accepts (lean, bark), lopes to 740 and holds; the sentry fixates and parks at ~700. Choice 1 with PRESS memory: WOLF visibly refuses (lean back, growl) and stays at the rubble. Choice 2: he watches. In the lane the eye strip is amber on patrol, snaps red with a rising servo when it detects the engineer (x > 545, within 180 px in its facing, not in the alcove) and chases at 230; it loses the engineer 2.5 s after they cross back over the rubble and never passes x 540.

beats.response: Clamp clack, tank falls on a 0.45 s tween, cable goes slack. MISS: dull clang, tank dents and vents a 3 s coolant-cloud hazard at 700, sentry snaps red and chases the panel (retreat left over the rubble), the arm rewinds for 6 s with a winch sound and re-hangs the tank. If WOLF was baiting and the drop missed, he breaks off and will not bait again this attempt.
beats.result: Hit: state.sentry_down = true, sentry becomes a prop, autosave C. Miss: transient only (arm rewinding, sentry chase then patrol).

beats.goal: Pop the exit bolt and leave.
beats.action: USE at the EXIT BOLT PANEL (x 850), then USE at the hatch (x 880).
beats.response: 0.6 s rising electrical whine, arc flash 120 ms, trauma 0.8, sparks from the junction box, bolt drops with a heavy clank, hatch slides open. final_options.name: COOLANT GALLERY: jump, push, time the vents (physical slice)
final_options.pitch: A third 960-px room right after the Records exit where the coolant line the pair argued about at the breaker finally ruptures. One boom drops a conduit block into the room and two floor vents start cycling. The engineer learns to jump on a safe step, pushes the block across live vents on their rhythm, climbs it to a ledge they cannot jump, and cranks the shutoff. WOLF can leap the ledge the engineer cannot and may pull the shutoff early if he chooses; only the engineer can push. Every contact (land, push, hit, crank, burst) has a sound, a shake and a real state change. Failing is a coolant burst that knocks the engineer back and resets only the current beat. This is the option that adds a permanent new verb.

final_options.name: PURGE SWEEP: Service Spine (stealth and timing slice)
final_options.pitch: A third 960-px room right after the Records exit. The moment the pair step out, a shutter slams behind them, a 90 s purge clock starts in the top card, and a sweep unit drops from a ceiling vent to clear the passage. The engineer hides in alcoves, times the patrol, holds USE to cut the unit's rail power (which drops it with a crunch and also unlocks the far hatch), then crosses two purge jets to the exit before the clock hits zero. WOLF runs ahead and finds the hatch sealed, and will draw the sweeper off once if asked; the engineer can always do it alone with hiding and timing. Getting caught or gassed costs only the current beat. This is the dread option: known threat, waiting, timing.

final_options.wolf_role: Independent, deterministic, never player-controlled. Beat 1 he runs to the hatch first and finds it sealed (shows the objective without text). Beat 3, when asked while the engineer is hidden, he chooses to decoy once per attempt if the drone is up and he has not already; his line reads the relay memory for flavour only, no gating, so an earlier blunt choice is not punished twice. A second ask or choice 2 is a visible refusal. Beat 5 he crosses the jets ahead by his own timing rule. The engineer can do every objective alone; WOLF only shortens the window.
final_options.engineer_fallback: The patrol has a fixed 2.4 s facing-away window; alcove A is 300 px from the panel, 1.6 s at 190 px/s, so the panel is always reachable by timing alone. Cutoff and hatch are engineer-only interactions. Jets have a 0.3 s warn and 1.6 s idle, crossable at walk speed. The 90 s clock allows roughly 2.5x the minimum route, so a cautious solo run finishes.
final_options.fail_and_retry: Two triggers: caught (drone within 24 px while unhidden and chasing) and purged (jet burst overlap, or clock at 0). Sequence: hit-stop 70 ms, white flash then red, trauma 1.0, short rumble, 0.5 s fade on IntroFade, then restore from the beat anchor: human and WOLF positions, drone reset to its patrol start, cutoff ticks, jet clocks, hidden false, wolf_decoy_used false, and sweep_clock set back to the value captured at that beat's start (never lower, so a run cannot become unwinnable). Memory and Records state untouched. Control returns within 1 s with hold-to-move still honoured. Anchors are transient; quitting mid-room resumes at the room-entry autosave, stated in the docs. No retry counter.
mechanics_new: SweepClock RefCounted: advance(delta), remaining, phase normal/urgent/expired, paused while paused, waiting_for_choice or chapter_close; pure logic.
Patroller Node2D: states patrol/chase/lost/dead, facing, Polygon2D cone, Area2D catch; detection = engineer within 220 px in facing and not hidden; constants only.
Hiding: two Area2D alcoves plus a transient hidden flag read by _update_controls() and the patroller; USE toggles in, any move steps out.
Held interaction: cutoff ticks every 0.4 s while interact is held in range; ticks persist on release and drive real rail-segment lights.
JetHazard cycle RefCounted (warn/burst/idle) plus Area2D + CPUParticles2D per grate; WOLF's mover consults is_dangerous().

feedback: Shutter close, rail segments going dark, drone drop, hatch lock light red -> amber -> open, and the stopped clock are all real state reads; nothing is a progress bar.
Hidden: sprite darkens and steps back, hint changes, cone sweeps over without turning red.
Detection: cone amber (patrol) / red (chase) / off (dead); chase chirp pitch rises.
Cutoff: one rail segment per tick and a click per tick, so partial progress is visible and survives release.
Jets: 0.3 s pre-warn blink and particle ramp before every burst so deaths feel earned.
Clock under 20 s: chirp interval shortens and the tint pulses; on success the clock freezes at its true value.
Fail: hit-stop + flash + shake + fade then instant control; WOLF resets to the anchor with the engineer so the pair are always together on retry.
Reduced Motion disables shake and hit-stop; flashes drop to a single 0.1 s tint change.

Touch: hold Left/Right, USE (tap or press-and-hold; the existing action_press on down / release on up already supports holding), Choice 1/2 replace the row during the choice. judged.recommendation: Build the shared foundation first and prove it in the rooms that already exist (give the relay spark and the door opening real shake, hit-stop, flash and a procedural clank on day one), then build Option A, BLOWBACK, trimmed to two booms plus the bolt with the lights-out aftermath as the cut line. It is the most direct answer to the user's ask (loud, state-changing booms rather than more stills), it adds zero input actions so the mobile budget stays at hold-to-move plus USE, every tool is engineer-operated so the WOLF rule and the fallback rule hold by construction, and its retry reuses _load_game/_sync_scene instead of a new transient-anchor system, which is the least new code for a fail state. Option B, COOLANT GALLERY, is the right pick instead if the user wants the game to gain a permanent new verb (jump) that later rooms will reuse, and Option C, PURGE SWEEP, if dread matters more than spectacle; both are good and both cost more new systems or more tuning risk than A. Whatever is chosen, nothing has been hands-on played yet, so the plan must end with a play pass and a device run before any feel claim, per AGENT.md.
